title: manifest.jsonl — Abhilekh Patal (National Archives of India) catalogue record
description: One archival description from the National Archives of India's Abhilekh Patal catalogue (REQ-0021). This is a CATALOGUE record, never a document: search and metadata are open, but the scanned records sit behind a paid reproduction-ordering flow (the results page carries Cart/Order markup and the site publishes a cancellation/refund policy), so `status` is always `metadata_only` and there is no dest or sha256. A `downloaded` status here would misdescribe what was acquired. Acquisition requires India-region egress — the AWS WAF answers other clients with HTTP 202 and a Human Verification page, which a headless browser does not clear either; the probe raises on that response rather than recording an empty corpus. `identifier` is the archive's own reference (e.g. MF_222400148993) and is the join key to a physical holding; `year` is the record's date as the archive states it, which for archival material is frequently absent. Any card label the site adds beyond the mapped set is preserved verbatim under `extra` rather than dropped.

item_id.description: The archive's own item UUID, lower-cased. Stable identity for the record.

identifier.description: The archive's reference number for the holding, e.g. MF_222400148993.

year.description: Null is common and meaningful: archival material is frequently undated in the catalogue.

extra.description: Card labels outside the mapped set, kept verbatim so a new field the archive introduces is not silently discarded.

search_query.description: The query that surfaced this record. Provenance: this catalogue is acquired by search, not by enumeration, so the query is part of how the record was found.

status.description: Always metadata_only for a real run. The documents are not publicly downloadable.

user_agent.description: The identity presented when this record was acquired. Recorded because the site's WAF challenges every commoner-probe User-Agent, so acquiring the catalogue requires choosing an identity deliberately — the corpus carries that choice rather than hiding it.
